contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you wrote a topic sentence. Today, add the details that tell more about it!

Supporting details are 2-3 sentences that tell more about your topic sentence — specific reasons, examples, or facts, not just repeating the topic sentence in different words. If your topic sentence is 'Summer is my favorite season,' a good supporting detail might be 'I get to go swimming almost every day.' A weak detail would just repeat the idea, like 'Summer is really fun.' Write 2 supporting details for the topic sentence you wrote yesterday.
You just added real supporting details to your paragraph! Tomorrow we'll learn the last piece: a closing sentence.

objectives: Distinguish a specific supporting detail from a vague, repetitive one
Write 2 supporting details that connect to a given topic sentence
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Read yesterday's topic sentence together.
2. Introduce supporting details via the summer/swimming example, contrasting with the vague 'really fun' example.
3. Have the child write 2 supporting details for their own topic sentence.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's closing-sentence lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: ask 'why' or 'can you give an example' questions out loud to help generate a specific detail
Ready for more: ask the child to write a third supporting detail
Watch specifically for details that just restate the topic sentence — that's the most common error at this stage, gently redirect toward something new and specific
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended writing activity — check that each supporting detail is specific and connects to the child's own topic sentence, not just a restatement of it.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 2 Writing standard W.2.1/W.2.2 (supplying reasons/facts that support the topic), continuing this week's one-paragraph build.

generationData.instructions: Write 2 supporting details for your topic sentence from yesterday.
